welsh.evidence: The eleven_v3 and eleven_v3_conversational language lists end "...Vietnamese (vie), Welsh (cym)." Welsh is absent from the eleven_multilingual_v2 list of 29 and therefore from eleven_flash_v2_5 (which is those 29 plus hu, no, vi).
welsh.rationale: Welsh survives on the model we do NOT use. Both live code paths hardcode a model with no Welsh: services/tts-service.cjs:265 sends model_id eleven_multilingual_v2, services/elevenlabs-service.cjs:120 defaults to eleven_flash_v2_5. Reaching Welsh means moving to eleven_v3 — which is also the model whose own docs advertise variability. Conditional, not survives: the vendor lists the language, the estate cannot currently render it, and the model that can is the least repeatable of the three.

eleven_multilingual_v2 (29): English (USA, UK, Australia, Canada), Japanese, Chinese, German, Hindi, French (France, Canada), Korean, Portuguese (Brazil, Portugal), Italian, Spanish (Spain, Mexico), Indonesian, Dutch, Turkish, Filipino, Polish, Swedish, Bulgarian, Romanian, Arabic (Saudi Arabia, UAE), Czech, Greek, Finnish, Croatian, Malay, Slovak, Danish, Tamil, Ukrainian, Russian
eleven_flash_v2_5 (32): all eleven_multilingual_v2 languages plus hu, no, vi
version_pinning: Model versions ARE pinnable by model_id — eleven_v3, eleven_multilingual_v2, eleven_flash_v2_5 are stable string ids and the docs carry an explicit "Deprecated models" table (eleven_turbo_v2_5 and eleven_turbo_v2 are marked deprecated with a named successor). That is better than Azure on paper. What is NOT pinnable is the OUTPUT: pinning the model id does not pin the audio, because the model itself is documented as sampling with randomness. A pinned model with an unpinned sampler is not repeatability.
cloning_consent: Two tiers, very different. Instant Voice Cloning: self-asserted only — you "confirm that you have the right and consent to clone the voice" with a tickbox. Professional Voice Cloning: own-voice-only, enforced by a live verification recording — "For now, we only allow you to clone your own voice", and in the FAQ, "Even with their consent, you cannot clone someone else's voice." A third party who wants to give you their PVC must create and verify it on their own account and share it by link. For SSi that means an Aran or Catrin professional clone must be made by Aran and Catrin, on their own accounts, and shared to us — not made by us from their existing recordings.

controls.seed: EXISTS but is explicitly not a guarantee. Verbatim from the API reference: "If specified, our system will make a best effort to sample deterministically, such that repeated requests with the same seed and parameters should return the same result. Determinism is not guaranteed. Must be integer between 0 and 4294967295." We send no seed anywhere in the estate.
controls.temperature: No temperature parameter. The equivalent knob is stability, verbatim: "Determines how stable the voice is and the randomness between each generation. Lower values introduce broader emotional range for the voice. Higher values can result in a monotonous voice with limited emotion." Default 0.5. In eleven_v3 it becomes a three-way choice — Creative ("More emotional and expressive, but prone to hallucinations"), Natural ("Closest to the original voice recording"), Robust ("Highly stable, but less responsive to directional prompts but consistent, similar to v2").
controls.other: similarity_boost (default 0.75) — "Determines how closely the AI should adhere to the original voice when attempting to replicate it." style (default 0) — style exaggeration, extra compute and latency if non-zero. use_speaker_boost (default true) — boosts similarity at a latency cost. speed 0.7-1.2 (default 1.0), "Extreme values may affect the quality". Pronunciation: up to 3 pronunciation_dictionary_locators per request (CMU/IPA rules), and in v3 raw IPA inline between forward slashes — with the caveat that "V3's IPA support achieves 80-90% pronunciation consistency". Continuity: previous_text/next_text and previous_request_ids/next_request_ids (max 3) to stitch long jobs. apply_text_normalization auto|on|off.

self_host: No. Cloud API only. No self-hosted or on-prem option is offered on any plan; Enterprise buys elevated concurrency and priority, not a local model.
pricing: Subscription-with-character-allowance, roughly $0.10 per 1,000 characters on eleven_v3 and eleven_multilingual_v2 (~$100 per 1M characters) and ~$0.05 per 1,000 on Flash/Turbo and v3 Conversational. Plans: Starter $6 (10k chars), Creator $22 (220k), Pro $99 (990k), Scale $299 (2.99M), Business $990 (9.9M). About 6-7x Azure and xAI per character on the model that can actually speak Welsh.
rate_limits: Concurrency-based, by plan, not requests-per-minute. Multilingual v2 / Flash concurrent request limits: Free 2/4, Starter 3/6, Creator 5/10, Pro 10/20, Scale 15/30, Business 15/30, Enterprise "Elevated". Over the limit requests queue rather than fail, typically adding ~50ms. Responses carry current-concurrent-requests and maximum-concurrent-requests headers.

live_integration.endpoint: POST https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/text-to-speech/{voiceId}, header xi-api-key, Accept: audio/mpeg (services/tts-service.cjs:252-262; services/elevenlabs-service.cjs:13 + :133).
live_integration.settings_we_send: text; model_id — HARDCODED eleven_multilingual_v2 on the tts-service path (services/tts-service.cjs:265) and defaulted to eleven_flash_v2_5 on the elevenlabs-service path (services/elevenlabs-service.cjs:120); voice_settings { stability: 0.5, similarity_boost: 0.75, style: 0, use_speaker_boost: true } (services/tts-service.cjs:266-271, defaults at :239-241). voiceId is the raw ElevenLabs voice id; voice-config-service reads it from voice_config.voiceId (services/voice-config-service.cjs:449). Note that generateElevenLabs accepts a `speed` config value (services/tts-service.cjs:241) and then never puts it in the body — the parameter is destructured and dropped.
live_integration.determinism_notes: We do the worst available thing on every determinism axis. No seed is sent — the string "seed" does not appear in any ElevenLabs request body in this repo, so we get fresh sampling on every call and cannot reproduce a clip we have already shipped. stability sits at the 0.5 default, which the vendor describes as the middle of a randomness dial. use_speaker_boost is on, which the vendor says increases compute. No pronunciation_dictionary_locators are ever attached, so there is no pronunciation override layer at all. No previous_text/next_text, so a long text split across requests has no continuity anchor. output_format is left to the default and the audible-response gate then hardcodes an assumption of 128 kbps (services/tts-service.cjs:282-285) — if the account default ever changed, that floor would be wrong. Finally the two code paths disagree about which model the estate uses, and neither model can speak Welsh.

gaps: The classic (non-v3) prose descriptions of stability and similarity now redirect to v3 content on the docs site; the numeric semantics quoted here come from the API reference parameter table, which is authoritative but terser than the old guide.

ElevenLabs publishes no statement about whether eleven_v3 output drifts across MODEL updates within the same model_id, only that sampling is nondeterministic within a version. That is the exact question axis E asks and the vendor does not answer it.
No phase-2 measurement was run: the seed "best effort" claim is untested. Whether same-seed output is byte-identical, perceptually identical, or neither is unknown and is a named phase-2 item.

ELEVENLABS_API_KEY is present in .env and now has the correct sk_ prefix (51 chars), which contradicts the 2026-08-17 note in tools/a108/a131-blind-raw-tts.cjs:44-47 that the stored value was a key ID rather than a key. The key was NOT exercised — phase 1 spends zero — so "present and correctly shaped" is all that is established.
Basque (eus) and Maltese (mlt) are absent from every ElevenLabs model list. Both are live estate languages.
Cantonese (yue) is absent — the v3 list names only Mandarin Chinese (cmn).
